title: agentic.config
description: How a repository works for an agent. `.ai/agentic.config.json` is committed; `.ai/agentic.config.local.json` overrides it on one machine and may tighten `guardrails` but never loosen it. A key neither file sets is inferred: the Node package manager from the lockfile, the `conventional` commit preset, and `gate.command` from the manifest's `check` script. Unknown top-level keys are tolerated so other tool families can share the file; the keys named here refuse unknown children.

baseBranch.description: The branch pull requests target; `auto` reads the remote's default branch.

node.description: Inferred from the lockfile. The package-manager guard refuses the other Node package managers only when this is `pnpm`.

ruby.description: Accepted so a repository can declare it; no guard reads it and nothing infers it.

guardrails.description: Policy the local override may tighten and never loosen. Every enum lists its strictest value first.

forcePush.description: `deny` refuses every force push. `lease` lets `--force-with-lease` and `--force-if-includes` through to a branch outside `protectedBranches`; bare `--force` and `-f` stay refused. `ask` is `lease` with a permission prompt for each lease push it lets through. Strictest first: deny, ask, lease.

commitOnProtected.description: `deny` refuses a `git commit`, `merge`, `cherry-pick` or `revert` on a branch listed in `protectedBranches`, so every change starts on a branch of its own. `allow` lets it through, for a repository that commits small fixes on its protected branch and pushes them from a person's terminal. Default `allow`. Strictest first: deny, allow.

envFiles.description: Which env files (`.env`, `.env.*`, `.envrc`) an agent may read, edit or write. A candidate is judged in this order: listed in `deny` → refused; listed in `allow` → readable; `policy` `deny` → refused; `policy` `git` → readable when git tracks it, refused when git ignores it or does not know it. Entries are globs against the path relative to the repository root: `*` and `?` as in a shell pattern (`*` crosses `/`), a leading `**/` means at any depth, so `.env` is the one in the root and `**/.env.example` every file of that name. No brace groups. A path outside the repository root, or outside any repository, is judged by its basename against the `**/` entries alone. Defaults: policy `git`, allow the `.env.example`, `.env.sample` and `.env.template` names anywhere, deny nothing. The local override may drop `allow` entries and add `deny` entries, never the reverse.

policy.description: What decides a candidate no list names. `deny` refuses it; `git` asks git: tracked passes, ignored or unknown is refused.

allow.description: Globs of the env files that are readable regardless of `policy`.

deny.description: Globs of the env files that are refused regardless of `policy`; wins over `allow`.

protectedBranches.description: Branches the guards refuse every push to: plain, lease or force. Under `commitOnProtected: deny` they refuse a commit, merge, cherry-pick or revert on one too. The local override may add to this list, never remove from it.

convention.description: The subject preset `pattern` falls back to. `ticket-key`: `[KEY-123] type: subject`, the tracker's key in brackets before a type from a fixed list. `conventional`: Conventional Commits; inferred when no layer sets either.

pattern.description: POSIX ERE the commit subject must match; set, it wins over `convention`. `grep -E` runs it, so no `\d`, `\s`, `\w`, `\b` or `(?…)`. `.+` accepts any subject.

trailer.description: A trailer key, such as `Co-Authored-By`, that every commit message must carry on a line of its own.

gate.description: The Gate `dw-sdlc gate` runs: the Steps under `steps` in order, then every Check under `checks`.

command.description: The one command that runs the Gate, the same in a terminal and in CI. Inferred as `pnpm check` where `package.json` has a `check` script.

steps.description: The Steps: toolchain commands run in order from the repository root through `sh -c`, each one's output passed through; the first that fails ends the Gate and no Check runs. A command the shell cannot find (exit 127) or execute (126) means the Gate cannot run.

checks.description: The Checks the Gate runs after its steps, every one even when another fails. A key names a Check the package ships, and a name it does not ship is refused.

run.description: The repository's own scripts, each run like a Step and reported as a Check under its `name`: exit 0 passes, 127 or 126 means the Gate cannot run, any other code fails.

name.description: The Check's name, which each of its failure lines carries: lowercase words joined by hyphens.

setup.description: Commands a fresh linked worktree needs before work starts. Reported at session start, not run.
